note: The Royal Society's five-page summary of its 29 October meeting. Ben Green called it “a summer like no other in mathematics”; James Maynard called OpenAI's quasi-Riemann hypothesis proof “the most important result in the analytic number theory for 100 years”; Martin Hairer expected many more long-standing questions to be answered within months; Ana Caraiani described the Association for Human Mathematics; panels discussed sifting AI papers, auto-formalised refereeing, new forms of credit and pressures on PhD students and postdocs; Timothy Gowers called for a contingency plan for mathematics as a profession. Licensed CC BY.
title: Mathematics in the age of AI: summary note
who: The Royal Society (meeting organised by Ben Green (Oxford) and Jon Keating (Oxford))
